What is Disney’s Monstober?

Monstober was Disney’s annual Halloween celebration, a month-long parade of spooky specials, monster-filled series, and fan-favorite family scares. What started as a Disney Channel programming event grew into a streaming tradition that spanned Disney Channel, Disney Jr., and beyond. These days, Disney+ is the place for the spine-tingling fun, with seasonal playlists that stack Halloween episodes, movies, and throwbacks in one spot. Whether your crew wants vampires, witches, or a pup-powered construction crew in costume, there’s something here for every age and scare tolerance. item.title: Fubo Adds New NHL Regional Sports Networks in These Four Markets
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: Fubo, a live TV streaming service, made a deal with the NHL to carry four new regional sports networks just in time for the 2026–2027 season.
item.content:encoded:
Carolina, Columbus, Minnesota, and St. Louis games will stream on Fubo

The shutdown of FanDuel Sports Network and Victory+ left many NHL teams scrambling to find new broadcast partners before the 2026–2027 season started. When the dust settled, four of those teams started their own regional sports networks and partnered with Amazon Prime Video for streaming distribution.

Now, add Fubo to the list of services that will carry games from the Carolina Hurricanes, Columbus Blue Jackets, Minnesota Wild, and St. Louis Blues in their respective markets.

“The addition of these RSNs to our already robust local sports coverage means Fubo subscribers can continue to enjoy their favorite local teams despite recent shifts in sports rights ownership,” Todd Mathers, executive vice president of content strategy and acquisition at Fubo, said in a statement.

Hurricanes Hockey Network, Blue Jackets Hockey Network, Wild+, and Blue Note+ join Fubo’s offering of NHL content that includes NHL Network, ESPN, ABC, and other RSNs. Those four new networks will be available to eligible Fubo subscribers.

By signing up, you agree to our Privacy Policy & Terms and Conditions.

CableTV.com verdict: Fans in these four NHL markets can breathe a sigh of relief

In early September, the NHL announced that Prime Video would stream local games for six teams “exclusively.” Those teams included the Hurricanes, Blue Jackets, Wild, and Blues.

What’s interesting about those four teams is that fans only need a free Amazon account to access RSNs — no need to pay for Prime. That drastically reduces the cost for those fans specifically.

But Fubo entering the mix makes things interesting. Not only does it significantly water down Amazon’s streaming exclusivity over these four RSNs, but it also gives fans a seamless experience if they already have Fubo. No need to create yet another account. In that sense, fans win.

Fubo wins as well. It’s one of the only live TV streaming services with a wide offering of regional sports networks. And now it won’t get left behind with all the recent changes to the NHL broadcasting landscape.

What do real customers think of GFiber and AT&T Fiber?

GFiber and AT&T Fiber specs and features: Gear, data, and more

Download speeds and pricing are a big part of any internet shopping decision, but they’re not the only factors worth considering. Here’s what else you get with AT&T Fiber and GFiber.

Free Wi-Fi equipment

Both AT&T Fiber and GFiber internet plans come with a free Wi-Fi gateway, which connects your home to the internet and works like a combo router/modem. GFiber utilizes a mesh Wi-Fi setup for full-home coverage. If your home isn’t set up for fiber internet, AT&T Fiber and GFiber will install an Optical Network Terminal (ONT) mounted to a wall inside.

GFiber and AT&T Fiber deals

GFiber doesn’t offer many deals, but sometimes you can get discounts on other Google services, like cloud storage. Check out GFiber’s website to see if you can dig up a deal or discount. AT&T regularly offers deals like free gift cards and discount codes for new fiber internet customers. Qualifying AT&T Wireless customers can also save $20 monthly on AT&T Fiber. Check out our AT&T deals guide for this month’s best AT&T deals.

AT&T Fiber has no contract, equipment, or data overage fees, so you’ll get straightforward monthly pricing. AT&T also offers free installation, but you may have to pay an additional fee if you initially decline and later request technical support.

Unlimited data

GFiber and AT&T Fiber include unlimited data with each of their plans, with no caps on either. You’ll be able to stream, download, and upload content with no overage fees, ever. For context, we don’t give any of our Editor’s Choice Awards to ISPs that ding you for data overages.

Phone and internet bundles

You can add VoIP (voice over internet protocol) home phone service to either AT&T Fiber or GFiber internet plans for an additional monthly fee. GFiber’s single home phone is a flat $10 a month, whereas AT&T offers several bundle plans starting at $24.99, as well as AT&T Wireless mobile plans. We give AT&T the edge here since you can score a bundle discount when you add a wireless plan. Who needs VoIP anyway?

What to look for in a home internet service

Some internet services have exciting deals and freebies that look super impressive. But when you want the best home internet provider, make sure the bang for your buck, reliability, features, and customer satisfaction ratings meet your standards before you sign a contract.

Bang for your buck

Since there’s no standard for internet pricing, even budget plans can run anywhere from $19.99 to $50.00 per month. (It’s a big range, we know.) Value depends a lot on your providers and location, but we used a few factors to determine which ISP offers the best internet value. Nearly all of our top internet service providers have no annual price increases. We wish that was the case for every ISP out there, but that’s not yet reality. Other ISPs will hike up the price after a year of service, making your once affordable plan much pricier than what you originally were paying. We also prioritize providers that are transparent with any extra fees that may be incurred—like, say, potential installation or router rental fees—along with providers that have a simple pricing method with all fees included.

Reliability

Our internet usage is growing all the time, and our bandwidth needs are higher than ever. With that in mind, you need internet that’s consistently fast and stable at your home. As part of our annual Internet Customer Satisfaction Survey series, we talked to thousands of real-life internet customers to see how they felt about their ISPs. Their feedback on their ISP’s speed and reliability (which refers to how often their internet goes down) played a huge role in our rankings. Two of our five top choices for best ISPs are fiber providers, which deliver more reliability than a cable, satellite, 5G, or DSL internet provider.

Features

Internet service providers are in the business of offering way more than internet these days. We gave the highest marks to ISPs that offered the best catalog of add-ons, which can include a number of options. Bundle choices were a huge plus in our eyes, as many offer services ranging from TV service to cheaper cell phone plans. We didn’t talk about data caps much in this article because most of our top recommendations offer unlimited data. We also favored ISPs that offered free equipment options. Most ISPs will give you the option to rent your equipment for a monthly fee or potentially buy it outright upfront. Even better, some providers, like gFiber and T-Mobile 5G Home Internet, won’t charge you at all. If equipment isn’t free, we suggest buying your wireless router instead of renting one since you’ll save on monthly rental fees.

Customer satisfaction

Customer service takes into account how efficiently ISPs get their customers the help they need. Some providers have their customer service desks staffed 24/7, while some process all requests through support pages and emails. Some ISPs are national chains with stores across the country to drop into, while others are largely online affairs. Regardless of how they solve customers’ problems, we prioritize how consistently and efficiently they do so, and our top picks all scored high marks on our survey.

Why you should trust us

To find this year’s best internet providers, we spent thousands of hours analyzing each ISP’s plans based on factors including price, reliability, and features like a free modem/router. We also relied on our annual internet customer satisfaction survey to find out how current customers felt about their ISPs. item.title: 5 Tips to Up Your Internet Game and Ditch Buffering Ahead of Football Season
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: Football season is here, which means that your weekends are probably full with fantasy football roster updates, games, and chicken wing deliveries.
item.content:encoded:
Football season is here, which means that your weekends are probably full with fantasy football roster updates, games, and chicken wing deliveries. But nothing ruins a good weekend of football games more than a slow internet connection. Buffering occurs when your streaming device pauses to load more video data due to insufficient bandwidth—and it always seems to happen at the worst moment. Want to make sure you don’t miss a single touchdown? Here are five great tips to speed up your internet connection to make sure your football games remain buffer-free this fall.
Quick answer: To eliminate buffering during football season:
  1. Hardwire your TV with an Ethernet cable
  2. Upgrade to at least 300 Mbps internet speed
  3. Upgrade your WiFi equipment
  4. Extend coverage with a mesh network
  5. Replace outdated streaming devices

1. Hardwire your connection

Ethernet connections are more reliable than WiFi for streaming because they eliminate wireless interference and signal drops. Wi-Fi connections are convenient, but they can be prone to dropped or inconsistent signals in your home. If you can, run an Ethernet cable to your TV streaming equipment (whether it’s your TV set, streaming device, or gaming console) to ensure a consistent signal.

2. Upgrade your internet speed

More bandwidth ensures smoother streaming, especially in busy households. Internet speed isn’t everything when it comes to TV streaming performance. But if you’re in a household with a lot of internet users, more download and upload bandwidth will help your TV streaming connection maintain a smooth 4K signal. We’d recommend an internet plan with download speeds of at least 300 Mbps if you live with more than three heavy internet users. Providers like Xfinity have internet plans with speeds well above 1 Gbps, so you’ll have ample plan options to maximize your home internet and football watching experience.

3. Upgrade your Wi-Fi equipment

Outdated routers and modems can bottleneck your internet performance regardless of your plan speed. Sometimes, your internet problems can be internet hardware problems. If your router and modem are more than a few years old, they can bottleneck your home internet performance and cause device problems downstream. If you’re unfamiliar with Wi-Fi hardware and don’t want to deal with troubleshooting equipment, consider getting internet gear from your provider. Providers like Xfinity have hardware rental programs that will give subscribers a combo Wi-Fi router and modem for a small monthly fee.

4. Extend Wi-Fi with a mesh network

Mesh networks eliminate dead zones by distributing your WiFi signal across multiple access points. Having problems watching the game on your bedroom TV? Wi-Fi routers are better than ever, but a single router can hit its limits if you live in a larger multi-story home. Mesh devices like Xfinity’s WiFi Extenders are small nightlight-sized devices that plug into wall outlets and increase your internet network’s range. They’ll ensure that every corner of your home has a consistent Wi-Fi signal and steady streaming performance.

5. Upgrade your streaming device

Newer streaming devices support faster WiFi standards and process video more efficiently. TV streaming devices make it convenient to get your TV online, but like with any device, they can get outdated and underpowered over time. If your streaming stick is more than a few years old and has buffering problems alongside issues like slow loading speeds, consider upgrading to a more recent model for faster streaming and general performance. These upgraded devices also have support for faster Wi-Fi 7 performance, so you’ll experience smoother streaming if you also have a capable Wi-Fi router. Still relying on your TV’s built-in apps and frustrated by their performance? Providers like Xfinity offer devices like the Xumo Stream Box, which can speed up performance for live TV and streaming services for eligible customers.

Whether you’re streaming your favorite team or watching football from sunrise to sundown, a proper internet setup is crucial as the right playcall for a successful football weekend. With these tips, you’ll be ready to watch buffer-free football all weekend long.

Key takeaways

  • Ethernet connections provide more stable streaming than WiFi by eliminating wireless interference.
  • Households with multiple streamers should have at least 300 Mbps download speeds.
  • Upgrading routers and streaming devices every 3–5 years ensures compatibility with current WiFi standards.
  • Mesh networks extend reliable coverage to every room in larger homes.

Get Xfinity Internet

Streaming buffering FAQ

What internet speed do I need to stream live football games without buffering?

Most streaming apps require at least 25 Mbps download speeds for a steady 4K signal, but this bandwidth can become stretched if you have multiple internet connections in your home. For most households, we recommend an Xfinity internet connection with at least 300 Mbps download speed for the smoothest football streaming experience.

Why is hardwiring my TV better than using Wi-Fi?

Hardwiring a TV with Ethernet ensures that you have a consistent internet signal that won't be interrupted by Wi-Fi or network problems. This will also maximize reliability and significantly reduce latency.

What causes buffering during live sports?

Buffering during live sports typically results from insufficient bandwidth, WiFi interference, network congestion from multiple devices, outdated equipment, or distance from your router. Live sports streams are particularly demanding because they require consistent real-time data delivery. Xfinity offers good internet reliability.

Does a mesh network reduce buffering?

Yes, mesh networks reduce buffering by eliminating WiFi dead zones and providing consistent signal strength throughout your home. They're especially effective in larger or multi-story homes where a single router can't provide adequate coverage. Xfinity offers mesh accessories.

How often should I upgrade my Wi-Fi router or streaming device?

We generally recommend upgrading your router and streaming device every three to five years to ensure you have the maximum streaming and internet performance for your home. With a router and modem, you'll want to ensure your home is aligned on wireless internet standards like Wi-Fi 7. Streaming device upgrade factors include general slowness, app crashes, and the latest Wi-Fi hardware standards. Xfinity offers hardware upgrade options.

item.content:encoded:
It’s not just you; streaming prices are rising, fast

Almost every major streaming service has increased its prices several times in the last few years. It’s gotten to the point where yearly price hikes feel like the norm, but it’s easy to forget that it wasn’t always like this. Streaming used to be a cheap, dependable form of entertainment. Prices would stay steady for years at a time. But those days are over. We love streaming television here at CableTV.com, but we also want to hold entertainment platforms and conglomerates accountable. So I’ve compiled data on all of our favorite streaming services to see the bigger picture. Which streaming price increases are reasonable changes, and which are taking advantage of economic panic? Let’s find out.

Why trust us? Despite our company name, we love television in all its forms. (Cable-and-streaming-TV-dot-com just wouldn’t have the same ring.) Our entertainment experts have spent thousands of hours testing all of the best (and worst) streaming services, and hundreds more hours tracking and researching industry trends. It’s our job to keep an eye on everything the big corporate streamers get up to—so you can focus on enjoying your favorite shows.
Jump to:

Netflix pricing history

Netflix’s latest price increase went into effect in March 2026. Netflix currently offers three plans:

  • Netflix Standard with Ads ($8.99/mo., 2 streams)
  • Netflix Standard ($19.99/mo., 2 streams, no ads)
  • Netflix Premium ($26.99/mo., 4 streams, no ads)

Netflix broke its streaming service off from its DVD rental service in 2011 and stopped renting out DVDs altogether in 2023. Netflix Basic (1 stream) was discontinued in January 2025. All Netflix plans now provide at least two simultaneous streams.

Netflix’s streaming service began as a free perk for its DVD rental subscribers in 2007, but became a standalone option in 2011. Users could pay $7.99/mo. for Netflix’s full, ad-free library of television and movies. That price for a Standard subscription—that is, two streams and no ads—has steadily increased every few years since its inception. Netflix subscribers now have to make a choice: Pay over double what the original Netflix subscription cost to maintain their ad-free experience, or downgrade to Netflix Standard with Ads for a reasonable $8.99/mo. price tag. Of course, you could always upgrade to Netflix Premium for those coveted four streams. But $26.99/mo. is a lot, even considering inflation, and those four streams don’t guarantee you can share your password with anyone outside of your main household. That’s the hidden fee behind every Netflix subscription: Restricted password sharing. Standard subscribers can purchase one extra member for $6.99–$8.99/mo., and Premium subscribers can purchase two. Now the gap between plans has risen to a whopping $9 per month. Disney+’s price has risen astronomically since its inception. Where Netflix took about 14 years to double the price of its original plan, Disney+ did the same in just four. Rather than the steady increase over time to mirror inflation, it gives the impression that Disney is scrambling to recover costs (since cancelling and removing a bunch of shows didn’t seem to work). When I recommend Disney+, I’m not usually recommending the standalone streaming service. It just seems like too much money for too little content (unless you’re really passionate about Star Wars). That’s because it couldn’t be cheaper than the HBO cable channel, a premium add-on with a premium price tag, or its streaming predecessor, HBO Now, which only streamed HBO content. So unlike Disney+ and Peacock, HBO Max never had the chance to market itself as the cool, cheap, cable alternative. Instead, it began as a way for non-cable subscribers to watch WarnerMedia-owned content on demand. The “HBO” brand name promised high-quality, prestige entertainment and was bolstered by a library full of titles from all of WarnerMedia’s brands: DC, Turner Classic Movies, Cartoon Network, Adult Swim, Studio Ghibli, and more. But things went downhill after WarnerMedia merged with Discovery to form Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD). The two media giants’ streaming services, HBO Max and Discovery+, merged into the monosyllabic “Max.” Max lost its premium cable identity when it lost its HBO branding, and the platform was flooded with Discovery’s most popular reality shows. (Discovery+ continues to this day as a standalone service that features dozens of additional reality TV franchises and spinoffs.) Something really bothers me about the name change—WBD justified it with the claim that the HBO branding was scaring parents away. WBD wanted to welcome kids onto their platform. This should have been a slam dunk because WBD owns Cartoon Network. But instead of investing in animation and kids’ content, Max slowly removed popular CN titles from its library. WBD reduced spending on animation, shut down CN’s physical headquarters, and stripped away the station’s identity. Kids lost interest in Max. In 2025, WBD gave up on kids. It sold off “Sesame Street” to Netflix and “The Amazing World of Gumball” to Hulu, put the “HBO” back in “HBO Max,” and is desperately trying to claw back its standing as the place to find serious adult television.

Users would pay for higher-quality streaming and the privilege of a star-shaped badge. Crunchyroll started formally offering a premium membership by 2009. This predates Netflix’s streaming service; there was no blueprint for how these subscriptions should work. In addition to the standard credit card and PayPal payment methods, users could also pay for their memberships by physically putting a check in an envelope and sending it through the mail. It was a different era. Early Crunchyroll memberships would give members same-day simulcasts and access to 100% of Crunchyroll’s library. Free users would get simulcasts a week late, and access to “most” of Crunchyroll’s library. It’s hard to say exactly how much “most” is, and how that percentage has changed over time. None of its paid tiers have ads, and you get the full anime experience for a relatively low price. The higher tiers are just nice-to-haves, with bonus perks like video games and manga. Crunchyroll’s subscriber count has been booming in recent years, so this paywall strategy seems to be working for them. item.title: Why Your WiFi Router Matters More Than Your Plan Tier
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: When it comes to home internet, it’s next to impossible to get by these days without a good WiFi setup.
item.content:encoded:
When it comes to home internet, it’s next to impossible to get by these days without a good WiFi setup. But between remembering the differences between WiFi 6 and WiFi 7 or hunting for your router password, we won’t blame you if troubleshooting your Wi-Fi gear feels like a big headache. If you’re considering calling your ISP to upgrade your plan and solve your slow internet problems, don’t click that checkout button just yet. Here’s one thing most people don’t realize — your home’s slow download speeds could also be caused by your Wi-Fi router instead of your internet plan. Tired of wondering why your home Wi-Fi is so slow? Keep reading to learn more about maximizing your Wi-Fi router’s performance and how Wi-Fi performance takes more than setting and forgetting your hardware.

What goes into a home Wi-Fi setup?

Let’s say you’ve just gotten a premium 1 Gbps internet plan for your home. You’re ready to stream 4K videos and make family FaceTime calls to your heart’s content, but when you sit down, you still have slow video delays. This problem illustrates one of the most important parts of home internet networks: Your network is only as fast as its slowest part. Internet bandwidth is like a pipe, and your 1 Gbps internet plan won’t reach its full potential if a 100 Mbps router bottlenecks it. Let’s break down a few things you’ll need to know to get the most out of your Wi-Fi router.

Wi-Fi 5 vs. Wi-Fi 6 vs. Wi-Fi 7

Terms like Wi-Fi 6 or Wi-Fi 6E refer to the generation of Wi-Fi hardware in devices like Wi-Fi routers, smartphones, and streaming devices. Every progressive generation of Wi-Fi improves features like signal stability and download reliability. Wi-Fi technology is relatively backward compatible, so rest assured that you won’t have to replace all your internet equipment. For example, a Wi-Fi 5 laptop can still get online through a Wi-Fi 7 router. But keep in mind that this mixing and matching limits your device’s maximum download speeds. It’s a key reason why major ISPs like Spectrum offer hardware that eliminates this guesswork for subscribers. With Spectrum’s Advanced WiFi router, you’ll get Wi-Fi 7 support out of the box for stellar internet performance. Spectrum’s Wi-Fi 7 support offers benefits like having more devices connected to Wi-Fi at once, faster download speeds, and more bandwidth.

Understanding wireless frequency bands

The first step to better understanding your Wi-Fi router’s performance is learning about wireless frequency bands. Every modern router features the following bands with unique strengths and weaknesses:

  • 2.4 GHz: This older band has excellent range but slow maximum speeds. It’s best designed for utilities like smart home light bulbs or cameras.
  • 5GHz or 6GHz: These bands are commonplace with Wi-Fi 6, 6E, and 7 devices. On these bands, you’ll have much faster gigabit-grade maximum speeds. But you may hit your router’s range limits if you live in a larger multi-story home.

Routers like Spectrum’s Advanced WiFi router support all three bands, so you can ensure your home’s devices get the bandwidth and download speeds they need to succeed.

Wi-Fi router positioning

Wi-Fi routers are like a radio tower, and their broadcast range can be heavily affected by where you place them in your home. Factors ranging from your distance to the router to glass windows can cause your network performance to nosedive. If possible, place your router in a central and visible area of your home to maximize internet performance.

Do you need mesh equipment?

Modern Wi-Fi routers come equipped with an array of antennas and gear designed to maximize their range. But even the strongest router can reach its limits if you live in a large house with multiple floors. If your home’s upper floors or bedrooms struggle to get a steady Wi-Fi connection, you may need to pair your router with mesh Wi-Fi gear. Mesh Wi-Fi hardware acts as an extender to your router so that you can stretch your Wi-Fi signal even further. Mesh Wi-Fi systems like Spectrum’s WiFi Extenders support Wi-Fi 7 technology and work alongside the Advanced WiFi router to eliminate internet dead spots in your home.

Get Spectrum Internet

When does your internet plan matter?

To play devil’s advocate: While a bad router ruins a good plan, your internet plan tier isn’t completely irrelevant. Here are two key reasons why you’ll also need to consider your internet plan alongside your router:

  1. Upload speeds: Many budget plans have meager upload speeds at around 10 Mbps. If your household has multiple people taking video calls or uploading files, you’ll run into internet performance issues.By comparison, Spectrum’s plans offer upload speeds starting at 20 Mbps, so you’ll have ample upload room for anything you need.
  2. Pairing speed with needs: Figuring out what internet speed you need? In general, your speed requirements depend on how you use your home internet.200 or 300 Mbps plans will be fine for households that just check email and watch Netflix. 500 Mbps and above plans are better suited for gamers or work-from-home employees who need maximum internet performance.With download speeds that start at 500 Mbps, Spectrum offers great internet performance at affordable rates.

Why Wi-Fi routers matter

The recipe for a good home internet experience requires a few components: a router, a modem, a computer or other internet-enabled device, and an internet connection working together. If your Wi-Fi router is more than three to five years old and your internet connection is bogging down, consider upgrading to a new model or contacting your ISP to purchase or rent one of their models. With Spectrum’s network of local retail stores, included modem, and optional Advanced WiFi router, Spectrum makes it easy to have a smooth home Wi-Fi experience and keep your home online. 2. Position your router in a central part of your home
